messages:
sara: Noticed a subtle bug in the Ruby SDK paginator when combined with prefetch+warmup. On large embed runs customers see duplicated items and occasional stalled pages.

eli: Can you describe duplication pattern? Is cursor/state advancement happening twice?

sara: Repro is with PageSize=50 Prefetch=4 Warmup=true. After a 429 burst, the paginator resumes but some pages are re-requested (same cursor) and we emit duplicate embeddings downstream.

sara: Short log snippet: 
```
2026-03-20T15:02:10Z paginator.rb:235 fetch page=12 cursor="abc123" attempt=1
2026-03-20T15:02:11Z http.rb:142 response=429 retry-after=0.7
2026-03-20T15:02:12Z paginator.rb:240 spawn prefetch worker page=13 cursor="def456"
2026-03-20T15:02:13Z paginator.rb:235 fetch page=12 cursor="abc123" attempt=2
```

ran: Hmm looks like the retry path re-queues the same page without updating the shared cursor. Is paginator state per-worker or shared?

sara: In Ruby we created a per-worker cursor snapshot to make warmup independent; that was to avoid blocking the foreground iterator. But the snapshot isn't reconciled on retry success/failure which can lead to two workers emitting the same page if retries are scheduled and the foreground also fetches it.

eli: How do other SDKs do it? Parity check?

ran: Go and Python keep a central cursor and have prefetch workers ask for the next page index from a single atomic counter. That prevents duplicates. Ruby's snapshot approach was meant to reduce lock contention but now it's causing correctness issues under throttling. SDK parity gap.

ops-bot: alert: sdk.ruby.prefetch.duplicates detected env=customer-prod window=300s duplicates=38 :rotating_light:

eli: Immediate mitigation: set Prefetch=1 or disable Warmup. Also we can add a client-side duplicate filter as temporary band-aid (hash of item id) for customers with strict dedupe needs.

sara: Proposed fixes:
- switch Ruby prefetch to central atomic cursor allocation (match Go/Python)
- ensure retry paths reconcile with central cursor when retry resolves (either success or give up)
- emit metric sdk.ruby.prefetch.duplicate_events and sdk.ruby.prefetch.paused when we see >N 429s

ran: Also check auth refresh interplay. We had one case where token rotation triggered during warmup and retried requests used a refreshed token while in-flight ones failed and retried, creating overlapping ranges. We should gate warmup so token refresh doesn't run concurrently with prefetch startup.

eli: Good point. Add a jittered backoff for warmup startup so many customers onboarding simultaneously don't all warm up at the same second. That will smooth bursts.

sara: I'll open a PR: fix/ruby-prefetch-central-cursor. Changes: central cursor allocator, release invariant on retry (always decrement inflight before scheduling backoff), and unit test that simulates 429 on alternating pages to assert no duplicates.

ran: Add an integration test against staging that enables prefetch=4 and injects 429s from a mock server to validate behavior under retries.

ops-bot: suggested mitigations posted to onboarding-docs: "If you see duplication or stalls during bulk ingest, try prefetch<=2 and warmup=false until SDK patch is applied."

eli: Once PR is ready, we should do a patch release. Also coordinate with docs: include note about token-refresh frequency and recommend avoiding very frequent rotate intervals (<30s) during bulk ingest.

sara: Assigning issue to eng-devex, label=sdk-parity, severity=medium. I'll include repro gist and minimal test harness in the PR. Thanks all. :pray:
